sub_units.name: JDBC Basics
sub_units.content: JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) is a Java API that enables Java applications to interact with relational databases. It provides a standard interface for connecting to databases, executing SQL queries, and processing results. The JDBC architecture consists of the JDBC API (java.sql and javax.sql packages) and JDBC drivers that translate Java calls into database-specific protocols. Understanding the JDBC workflow — loading the driver, establishing a connection, creating statements, executing queries, and closing resources — is fundamental to database programming in Java.

videos.title: JDBC Basics
videos.ai_context: Video tutorial covering JDBC Basics in JDBC & Advanced Java Concepts.

sub_units.name: DriverManager & Connection
sub_units.content: The DriverManager class manages a list of database drivers and establishes connections to databases using the getConnection() method with a JDBC URL, username, and password. The Connection interface represents a session with a specific database and provides methods for creating statements, managing transactions, and retrieving metadata. JDBC URLs follow the format jdbc:subprotocol:subname. Understanding driver registration, connection string formats for different databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle), and proper connection management with try-with-resources is essential for reliable database connectivity.

videos.title: DriverManager & Connection
videos.ai_context: Video tutorial covering DriverManager & Connection in JDBC & Advanced Java Concepts.

sub_units.name: PreparedStatement
sub_units.content: PreparedStatement is a precompiled SQL statement interface that extends Statement, offering improved performance and security. It uses parameterized queries with placeholders (?) to prevent SQL injection attacks. Parameters are set using typed setter methods like setInt(), setString(), and setDate(). PreparedStatement is more efficient than Statement for repeated executions because the SQL is compiled once and reused. It supports batch operations via addBatch() and executeBatch() for executing multiple statements efficiently.

videos.title: PreparedStatement
videos.ai_context: Video tutorial covering PreparedStatement in JDBC & Advanced Java Concepts.

sub_units.name: ResultSet
sub_units.content: The ResultSet interface represents the result of a SQL query and provides methods to iterate over and retrieve data from the result rows. It uses a cursor that initially points before the first row, and the next() method advances it row by row. Data is retrieved using typed getter methods like getInt(), getString(), and getDate() by column name or index. ResultSet types include TYPE_FORWARD_ONLY, TYPE_SCROLL_INSENSITIVE, and TYPE_SCROLL_SENSITIVE, with concurrency modes for read-only or updatable results.

videos.title: ResultSet
videos.ai_context: Video tutorial covering ResultSet in JDBC & Advanced Java Concepts.

sub_units.name: Transaction Management
sub_units.content: Transaction management in JDBC ensures data integrity by grouping multiple SQL operations into a single atomic unit of work. By default, JDBC operates in auto-commit mode where each statement is committed individually. Disabling auto-commit with setAutoCommit(false) allows explicit transaction control using commit() to save changes and rollback() to undo them on failure. Savepoints provide partial rollback capability within a transaction. Understanding ACID properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) and isolation levels is critical for building reliable data applications.

videos.title: Transaction Management
videos.ai_context: Video tutorial covering Transaction Management in JDBC & Advanced Java Concepts.

sub_units.name: Connection Pooling
sub_units.content: Connection pooling is a technique that maintains a cache of reusable database connections to improve application performance and scalability. Creating database connections is expensive, so pools pre-create and manage a set of connections that are borrowed and returned by application threads. Popular connection pool libraries include HikariCP, Apache DBCP, and C3P0. Key configuration parameters include minimum/maximum pool size, connection timeout, and idle timeout. Understanding connection pooling is essential for building high-performance Java applications that interact with databases.

videos.title: Connection Pooling
videos.ai_context: Video tutorial covering Connection Pooling in JDBC & Advanced Java Concepts.

sub_units.name: Annotations
sub_units.content: Annotations in Java are metadata markers that provide information about code to the compiler, runtime, or development tools without directly affecting program logic. Built-in annotations include @Override, @Deprecated, @SuppressWarnings, and @FunctionalInterface. Java supports custom annotations defined with @interface and meta-annotations (@Target, @Retention, @Inherited, @Documented) to control their behavior. Annotations are widely used in frameworks like Spring, Hibernate, and JUnit for configuration, dependency injection, and testing.

videos.title: Annotations
videos.ai_context: Video tutorial covering Annotations in JDBC & Advanced Java Concepts.

sub_units.name: Enums & Inner Classes
sub_units.content: Enums in Java are special data types that define a fixed set of named constants, providing type safety and readability. Enums can have fields, constructors, and methods, and are implicitly final and extend java.lang.Enum. Inner classes are classes defined within another class, including member inner classes, static nested classes, local inner classes, and anonymous inner classes. Inner classes can access the enclosing class's members and are useful for logically grouping related classes, implementing callbacks, and creating concise event handlers.

videos.title: Enums & Inner Classes
videos.ai_context: Video tutorial covering Enums & Inner Classes in JDBC & Advanced Java Concepts.

sub_units.name: Garbage Collection
sub_units.content: Garbage collection in Java is an automatic memory management process that identifies and reclaims memory occupied by objects that are no longer reachable by the program. The JVM's garbage collector runs in the background, freeing developers from manual memory deallocation. Key concepts include the heap memory structure (Young Generation, Old Generation, Metaspace), garbage collection algorithms (Serial, Parallel, CMS, G1, ZGC), and object eligibility for garbage collection. The finalize() method and System.gc() provide limited control over garbage collection behavior.
